text:
ajay: Seeing sustained queue buildup on gpu-inference-prod around 09:12 UTC. HPA scaled pods from 4 -> 12 but Cluster Autoscaler didn't add GPU nodes, so most pods are Pending with Unschedulable. Noticed long model load times on evicted pods, so queue never drains. Anyone on call?

miriam: Oof. Do we have min-nodes set on the GPU nodepool?

ajay: Min is 0 for the spot gpu pool. Max at 50. CA logs show podUnschedulable but then 'no nodes available for requested resource'.

josh: Could be taints/tolerations or nodeSelector mismatch. Also CA sometimes refuses to scale if pod set has nodeAffinity that doesn't match any nodegroup.

ryan: Share pod spec?

ajay: Pasted snippet: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: gpu-inference}
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: nvidia-tesla-a100
  resources:
    limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  tolerations:
    - key: "gpu-pool"
      operator: "Exists"
```

marina: That nodeSelector label is wrong for our managed GPU nodegroup. The nodes are labeled `accelerator: a100-80gb` in us-west2. CA cannot propose a node if label mismatch.

ajay: Ah. That explains why pods remain Pending even though capacity exists in other nodegroups. But CA logs also show scale-up was attempted earlier and failed because of quota in us-west2 for GPUs.

sre-bot: incident:gpu-queue #1769991111 created - queue backlog > 2000 requests, service latency 1.8s -> 7.2s. Paging oncall-team.

miriam: We should fix label mismatch immediately, but longer term: HPA is scaling pods based on our custom metric (queue_length per pod) which works, but when scale->down occurs CA removes nodes and warms go cold. Model load is 30-45s per pod which kills p99.

josh: Two angles: reduce churn (keep warm capacity) or improve scheduling so pods land on warm nodes. Option: set gpu nodepool min size > 0 or use warm-pool feature if cloud provider supports it.

ryan: Also consider switching from HPA -> KEDA for queue-aware scaling so scale decisions take queue depth and can set cooldowns. But KEDA still relies on CA for nodes.

marina: Another quick mitigation: set HPA max to something that matches nodepool max pods per node so CA can plan; or use pod.preset to request less CPU initially so pods are schedulable on non-gpu pools? (not ideal)

ajay: For immediate fix I'm going to patch nodeSelector to `accelerator: a100-80gb` and bump min size of the dedicated-gpu-pool to 2. Will monitor.

sre-bot: deploybot: patch applied to gpu deployment (image unchanged).

miriam: Also: VPA in auto mode touched these pods last week? I remember a rollout that set cpuRequests lower which might trick CA's binpacking heuristics. VPA + HPA is tricky. Are we running VPA for this deployment?

josh: We have a VPA object in 'recommend' mode for most services. For gpu-inference we previously enabled 'auto' for a short experiment. If VPA reduces requests too low, CA might think pods are smaller and not trigger scale-up until it's too late, or scale down too aggressively.

marina: Check prometheus adapter config — our custom metric is exposed as `queue_length_per_pod`. HPA uses that via the adapter. There was also a bug where adapter reports aggregated metric with a delay, causing HPA reaction lag.

ajay: FYI output from `kubectl describe hpa gpu-inference`:
```
Metric: queue_length_per_pod (custom) target 10 current 68 -> desired replicas 13
Events: SuccessfulRescale -> desired=13 (current=4) at 09:14
```
But pods are Pending because CA couldn't find matching nodegroup earlier.

ryan: If CA sees unschedulable pods it will try to scale, but if your GPU quota is exhausted CA will stop. We should confirm cloud account GPU quota and whether other clusters/teams are using it. Also region constraints: we only have GPU quota in us-west2, and CA might be trying to spin up in us-east1 where we have zero quota. CA expander config can pick the wrong nodegroup if labels/regions ambiguous.

josh: Recommend setting CA flag `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? Not sure. More useful: tag nodegroups with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-up=true` and set explicit node-group priorities using labels + expander=priority. That reduces misrouting.

marina: Cost note: keeping min nodes >0 increases baseline costs. But trading that for lower p99 and fewer failed requests might be worth it for high-value customers. We should estimate delta: 2 a100 nodes ~ $X/hr. Compare to cost of retries and SLO penalties.

ajay: Patch is live: nodeSelector fixed, dedicated-gpu-pool min=2. CA now successfully scaled up one node and several Pending pods scheduled. Queue drained ~ 45% in 10m.

sre-bot: incident update: queue backlog reduced to 450, latency p99 1.6s.

miriam: Next steps (proposed):
- Lock nodeSelector to canonical label via admission webhook or PodPreset so future deploys don't diverge
- Set gpu nodepool min to 1 for prod, consider warm-pool for bursty workloads
- Disable VPA auto for gpu workloads; keep recommend only
- Add CA node-group priorities and ensure node labels/affinities match exactly
- Add a small deployment of GPU 'hot-warm' lightweight pods that keep model cache primed (or use shared model cache service)
- Investigate using KEDA with cooldowns and synchronous drains to prevent oscillation

josh: Also add PodPriority and PodTopologySpread to prefer scheduling on warm nodes with lower model loading times. And increase scaleDownDelay for CA (`--scale-down-unneeded-time`) for GPU groups.

ryan: I'll open a quick RFC to evaluate reserved vs spot for inference workloads. For now we should mark this incident as mitigated once queue < 50 and p99 under 1s.

marina: Agree. Also log cost impact in cost-channel.

ajay: Thanks all, I'll follow up with exact kube manifests and CA logs in the incident ticket.

miriam: Nice work catching the label mismatch. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident:gpu-queue #1769991111 resolved -> status: mitigated at 09:58 UTC
